bant1299.name: Bantu Layer Gulf Guinea Creole Portuguese

languages.name: Faeto and Celle San Vito Francoprovencal
Somray of Battambang-Somre of Siem Reap

arme1241.name: Armenian
arme1241.rationale: Holds Classical-Middle, Eastern and Western Armenian; WALS genus Armenian coincides (1/1 mapped) and Indo-European handbooks treat this branch as 'Armenian', parallel to 'Albanian' for alba1267 in this dataset.

azte1234.name: Aztecan
azte1234.rationale: The genus holds all Nahuatl varieties, Pipil and Pochutec, and matches WALS genus Aztecan (10 of 11 mapped members). "Aztecan" (or Nahuan) is the usual name for this branch of Uto-Aztecan; "Aztec" names a people, not a language group.

bant1295.name: North-West Bantu
bant1295.rationale: Bostoen explicitly applies this name to zone A plus B10/(20)/30, closely matching the genus. Membership is only approximate: treatments differ over Mbam and B20, so this is a provisional conventional label rather than a verified exact synonym.
bant1295.sources: Bostoen 2008, Bantu Spirantization: Morphologization, lexicalization and historical classification, p. 304, https://www.africamuseum.be/publication_docs/Bostoen%202008%20Diachronica.pdf; Bostoen and Grégoire 2007, La question bantoue: bilan et perspectives, https://backoffice.biblio.ugent.be/download/446279/8675570; Bostoen and Guérois 2022, Reconstructing suffixal phrasemes in Bantu verbal derivation, pp. 363–364, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7575829

boli1260.name: Bolivia-Paraná
boli1260.rationale: The genus holds Mojeño (Ignaciano, Trinitario), Baure, Paunaka, Apolista, Magiana and Terena-Kinikinao-Chané, and matches WALS genus Bolivia-Parana (3/3). Terena and Chané are spoken in Brazil and Argentina, so "Bolivian" is too narrow.
boli1260.sources: https://wals.info/languoid/genus/boliviaparana; Aikhenvald 1999, The Arawak language family, in Dixon & Aikhenvald (eds.) The Amazonian Languages

cent2060.name: Central Pacific
cent2060.rationale: Glottolog 'linkage' is a bookkeeping label. The group (Fijian, Rotuman and Polynesian) is called Central Pacific throughout the Oceanic literature.
cent2060.sources: https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/cent2060;Lynch, Ross & Crowley 2002, The Oceanic Languages;Geraghty 1983, The History of the Fijian Languages

east2703.name: Nyun-Buy
east2703.rationale: The genus holds the Bainounk (Nyun) varieties plus Buy (Kasanga, Kobiana); 'Nyun' alone normally denotes only the Bainounk cluster, whereas the specialist name for the whole group is Nyun-Buy.
east2703.sources: Pozdniakov & Segerer 2024, A genealogical classification of Atlantic languages, in Lüpke (ed.), The Oxford Guide to the Atlantic Languages of West Africa, sect. 'The Nyun-Buy cluster' (https://academic.oup.com/book/59850/chapter/511367287);https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/east2703

hung1287.name: Hungarian
hung1287.rationale: Holds only Hungarian and Old Hungarian; 'Hungaric' is a Glottolog formation, and the literature simply speaks of Hungarian (the Uralic handbook's Hungarian chapter covers its history).

kada1291.name: Kra
kada1291.rationale: Holds only the Kra branch (Eastern Kra and Southwestern Kra: Gelao varieties, Lachi, Laha, Buyang, Qabiao, En), but 'Kadai/Kadaic' is widely used for the whole Tai-Kadai (Kra-Dai) family; 'Kra' is the established name for this branch since Ostapirat (2000), which Glottolog itself cites for the node.
kada1291.sources: https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/kada1291;Ostapirat 2000, Proto-Kra, Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 23(1)

khan1279.name: Khanty
khan1279.rationale: Holds the Khanty varieties (Northern, Eastern/Surgut-Vach-Vasjugan, Southern) that Glottolog treats as languages; specialists call this group 'Khanty' (e.g. the Khanty chapter in the Uralic handbook), 'Khantyic' being a Glottolog formation.
khan1279.sources: https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/khan1279;Csepregi 2023, Khanty, in Abondolo & Valijärvi (eds.), The Uralic Languages, 2nd ed. (Routledge)

kora1297.name: Korap
kora1297.rationale: Drop the Glottolog 'linkage' label. The genus holds Arop-Lokep, Karnai, Malasanga and Mur Pano, which make up Ross's Korap group of Ngero-Vitiaz.
kora1297.sources: https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/kora1297;Ross 1988, Proto Oceanic and the Austronesian Languages of Western Melanesia;Lynch, Ross & Crowley 2002, The Oceanic Languages;https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_New_Guinea_languages

mans1269.name: Mansi
mans1269.rationale: Holds Northern, Central and Southern Mansi; specialists call this group 'Mansi' (e.g. the Mansi chapter in the Uralic handbook), 'Mansic' being a Glottolog formation.
mans1269.sources: https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/mans1269;Virtanen & Horváth 2023, Mansi, in Abondolo & Valijärvi (eds.), The Uralic Languages, 2nd ed. (Routledge)

mata1290.name: Maká-Nivaclé
mata1290.rationale: Mataguayo I is a Glottolog bookkeeping label. The genus holds Maká and Nivaclé, and the literature calls this proposed clade Maká-Nivaclé. Nikulin & Carol 2024 doubt that it is a clade.
mata1290.sources: Nikulin & Carol 2024, Historical phonology of Mataguayan (Language Science Press); https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/mata1290

mata1291.name: Wichí-Chorote
mata1291.rationale: Mataguayo II is a Glottolog bookkeeping label. The genus holds Wichí (Weenhayek, Güisnay, Vejoz) and Chorote (Forest and Riverine), the well-supported Wichí-Chorote (Chorote-Wichí) clade of Mataguayan.
mata1291.sources: Nikulin & Carol 2024, Historical phonology of Mataguayan (Language Science Press; https://zenodo.org/records/13907413); https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/mata1291

mund1335.name: Munda
mund1335.rationale: Holds the Munda languages (North Munda, Kharia, Juang, Sora-Juray-Gorum, Gutob-Remo, Gata'); all 9 WALS-mapped members of WALS genus Munda fall here, and 'Munda' is the universal name in the specialist literature, while 'Mundaic' is a Glottolog-only form.

narr1279.name: Talodi
narr1279.rationale: 'Narrow' is Glottolog bookkeeping distinguishing the group from older Talodi including Lafofa (Tegem, a separate genus here); the genus coincides with WALS genus Talodi (2/2) and is the group called Talodi in the specialist literature. Whole-family genus, hence medium.
narr1279.sources: https://wals.info/languoid/genus/talodi;Norton & Alaki 2015, The Talodi languages: a comparative-historical analysis, Occasional Papers in the Study of Sudanese Languages 11;https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/narr1279

nort2858.name: North Huon Gulf
nort2858.rationale: Drop the Glottolog 'linkage' label. The genus holds Bugawac, Kela and Yabem, which make up North Huon Gulf in Ross's Huon Gulf family.
nort2858.sources: https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/nort2858;Ross 1988, Proto Oceanic and the Austronesian Languages of Western Melanesia;Lynch, Ross & Crowley 2002, The Oceanic Languages

nucl1744.name: Nuclear Papuan Tip
nucl1744.rationale: Drop the Glottolog 'linkage' label. Keep 'Nuclear', which is part of Ross's established name and contrasts with Peripheral Papuan Tip. The genus holds the North Papuan Mainland-D'Entrecasteaux and Suauic languages.
nucl1744.sources: https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/nucl1744;Ross 1988, Proto Oceanic and the Austronesian Languages of Western Melanesia;Lynch, Ross & Crowley 2002, The Oceanic Languages

perm1256.name: Permic
perm1256.rationale: Holds Komi (Zyrian, Permyak, Yazva) and Udmurt, exactly WALS genus Permic (3/3 mapped); 'Permic' is the standard English term in Uralistics and avoids the geological sense of 'Permian'.

prea1240.name: Kampan
prea1240.rationale: The genus is exactly the Kampa/Campa languages (Asháninka, Ashéninka varieties, Caquinte, Machiguenga, Nanti, Nomatsiguenga). "Pre-Andine" in Aikhenvald's usage also covers Yanesha' (Amuesha), which is a separate genus here. WALS calls these 4/4 mapped members "Pre-Andine Arawakan", but specialists name the group Kampa(n).
prea1240.sources: Mihas 2017, The Kampa subgroup of the Arawak language family, in Aikhenvald & Dixon (eds.) Cambridge Handbook of Linguistic Typology (https://researchonline.jcu.edu.au/47586/); https://wals.info/languoid/genus/preandinearawakan

sout1516.name: South Bird's Head Proper
sout1516.rationale: The genus holds the South Bird's Head family minus Inanwatanic (Kaburi, Kais, Puragi, Kemberano, Kokoda/Arandai, Dombano); WALS calls exactly this group "South Bird's Head Proper" (its only WALS member, Arandai, is here), and plain "South Bird's Head" would wrongly suggest the whole family including Inanwatan.

taba1270.name: Tabar
taba1270.rationale: Drop the Glottolog 'linkage' label. The genus holds Lihir, Mandara and Notsi, Ross's Tabar group. Confidence is medium because 'Tabar' is also an alternative name of Mandara, a member language.
taba1270.sources: https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/taba1270;Ross 1988, Proto Oceanic and the Austronesian Languages of Western Melanesia;Lynch, Ross & Crowley 2002, The Oceanic Languages

tsim1258.name: Tsimshianic
tsim1258.rationale: The genus is the whole family (Nisga'a, Gitxsan, Coast/Southern Tsimshian) and matches WALS genus Tsimshianic (3/3). "Tsimshian" is also the name of one member language (Sm'algyax).
tsim1258.sources: https://wals.info/languoid/genus/tsimshianic; Mithun 1999, The Languages of Native North America (CUP); Campbell 1997, American Indian Languages

uncl1521.name: Caribbean Arawakan (unclassified)
uncl1521.rationale: This is a Glottolog bookkeeping node for Araicu and Uirina, which are left unclassified within Caribbean Arawakan. It is not a subgroup.

uncl1527.name: Indo-European (unclassified)
uncl1527.rationale: A Glottolog bookkeeping node for poorly attested Indo-European languages not placed in any branch (Dacian, Messapic, Thracian); it is not a subgroup.

unun9898.name: Maxakalian (unclassified)
unun9898.rationale: This is a Glottolog bookkeeping node for poorly attested Maxakalian languages (Capoxo, Koropó, Macuni) left unclassified within Nuclear Maxakalian. It is not a subgroup.

unun9910.name: Benue-Congo (unclassified)
unun9910.rationale: Glottolog pseudo-family node for languages unclassified within Benue-Congo (here Baissa Fali and Tita); it is not a subgroup, so the name should say so transparently.

unun9947.name: Southern Uto-Aztecan (unclassified)
unun9947.rationale: This is a Glottolog bookkeeping node for the poorly attested Coca and Jova, which are left unclassified within Southern Uto-Aztecan. It is not a subgroup.

unun9972.name: Rai Coast (unclassified)
unun9972.rationale: Glottolog bookkeeping node for Rai Coast languages without a subgroup assignment (Biyom, Tauya); it is not a subgroup, and the transparent name avoids implying one.
unun9972.sources: https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/unun9972; Pawley & Hammarström 2017, The Trans New Guinea family (in Palmer ed., The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area)

will1243.name: Willaumez
will1243.rationale: Drop the Glottolog 'linkage' label. The genus holds Bola, Bulu, Meramera and Nakanai, which make up Ross's Willaumez group of Meso-Melanesian.
will1243.sources: https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/will1243;Ross 1988, Proto Oceanic and the Austronesian Languages of Western Melanesia;Lynch, Ross & Crowley 2002, The Oceanic Languages;https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meso-Melanesian_languages

yuul1239.name: Yolngu
yuul1239.rationale: The genus is the whole Yolngu (Yolŋu Matha) group (Dhuwal, Djambarrpuyngu, Gupapuyngu, Gumatj, Ritharrngu, Djinang, Djinba, Dhangu, Dayi, Nhangu); specialists and Glottolog's own child node "Southern Yolngu" use the spelling Yolngu/Yolŋu, while "Yuulngu" is an older spelling.
yuul1239.sources: https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/yuul1239; Wilkinson 1991, Djambarrpuyngu: a Yolngu variety of northern Australia (PhD, Sydney); Bowern & Atkinson 2012, Computational phylogenetics and the internal structure of Pama-Nyungan, Language 88(4)
